name: 尼古拉·特斯拉
nationality: 美国/克罗地亚/奥匈帝国

points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 尼古拉·特斯拉于1856年7月10日出生在奥地利帝国克罗地亚斯米良的一个塞尔维亚东正教家庭。他的父亲是东正教牧师，母亲是一位受过教育的发明家。特斯拉从小就展现出非凡的记忆力和对数学的浓厚兴趣。童年时期，他经历了严重的疾病，但康复后展现出惊人的想象力，经常在脑海中构建复杂的机械装置。这段经历培养了他强大的视觉思维能力，成为他日后发明创造的重要基础。
points.descriptionEn: Nikola Tesla was born on July 10, 1856, in Smiljan, Croatia, then part of the Austrian Empire, to a Serbian Orthodox priest father and an educated inventor mother. From an early age, Tesla exhibited extraordinary memory and a keen interest in mathematics. As a child, he suffered from a severe illness but recovered with remarkable imagination, often visualizing complex mechanical devices in his mind. This experience developed his powerful visual thinking abilities, which became fundamental to his later inventions.

points.title: 欧洲突破
points.description: 1882年，特斯拉在布达佩斯电话公司工作期间，首次构思了交流电感应电动机的原理。这一突破性发现彻底改变了电力传输的方式。他描述了在公园散步时突然想到旋转磁场的原理，并在沙地上画出了设计图。这一时期，他还改进了电话中继器，并设计了第一台无电刷交流电动机。这些成就奠定了他在电气工程领域的声誉，为他后来前往美国奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1882, while working at the Budapest Telephone Exchange, Tesla first conceived the principle of the alternating current induction motor. This breakthrough discovery revolutionized power transmission. He described having a sudden revelation about rotating magnetic fields while walking in a park, sketching his design in the sand. During this period, he also improved telephone repeaters and designed the first brushless AC motor. These achievements established his reputation in electrical engineering and laid the foundation for his later move to the United States.

points.title: 爱迪生合作
points.description: 1884年，特斯拉带着推荐信前往美国，最初在托马斯·爱迪生的欧洲分公司工作。后来他加入爱迪生位于纽约的公司，负责改进直流发电机。尽管特斯拉做出了重要改进，但他与爱迪生在交流电与直流电的争论上产生分歧。爱迪生支持直流电系统，而特斯拉坚信交流电的优势。这段经历让特斯拉意识到需要独立发展自己的理念，为他后来与西屋电气的合作埋下伏笔。
points.descriptionEn: In 1884, Tesla traveled to the United States with letters of recommendation and initially worked for Thomas Edison's European operations. He later joined Edison's company in New York, improving direct current generators. Despite his significant improvements, Tesla clashed with Edison over the debate between alternating current and direct current systems. Edison favored DC, while Tesla firmly believed in AC's advantages. This experience made Tesla realize the need to develop his own vision independently, setting the stage for his later collaboration with Westinghouse.

points.title: 西屋电气时期
points.description: 1888年，特斯拉与乔治·威斯汀豪斯达成合作，后者购买了特斯拉多项交流电相关专利。在匹兹堡期间，特斯拉完善了他的多相交流电系统，包括电动机、变压器和发电机。1893年，在芝加哥世界博览会上，西屋电气公司使用特斯拉的交流电系统成功点亮了整个博览会，击败了爱迪生的直流电方案，标志着交流电的胜利。这一成就确立了特斯拉在电气工程领域的地位，并推动了交流电系统的广泛应用。
points.descriptionEn: In 1888, Tesla formed a partnership with George Westinghouse, who purchased many of Tesla's AC-related patents. While in Pittsburgh, Tesla perfected his polyphase AC system, including motors, transformers, and generators. In 1893, at the Chicago World's Fair, Westinghouse successfully powered the entire exhibition using Tesla's AC system, defeating Edison's DC proposal and marking a victory for alternating current. This achievement established Tesla's position in electrical engineering and drove the widespread adoption of AC systems.

points.title: 高能实验
points.description: 1895年至1899年，特斯拉在科罗拉多斯普林斯建立了实验室，进行高频高压电实验。他成功建造了大型变压器，产生了数百万伏特的电压，并研究了无线传输电力的可能性。在这里，他观察到了球状闪电和地球共振现象，并记录了闪电在远距离的传播。这些实验为他的无线通信和广播系统奠定了基础，也为后来的无线电发展提供了重要启示。特斯拉还声称接收到了来自太空的信号，这可能是他最早探索无线电天文学的尝试。
points.descriptionEn: From 1895 to 1899, Tesla established a laboratory in Colorado Springs where he conducted high-frequency, high-voltage experiments. He successfully built large transformers generating millions of volts and studied the possibility of wireless power transmission. Here, he observed ball lightning and Earth's resonance phenomena, documenting lightning propagation over long distances. These experiments laid the foundation for his wireless communication and broadcasting systems, providing important insights for later radio development. Tesla also claimed to have received signals from space, possibly his earliest attempt at radio astronomy.

points.title: 晚年创新
points.description: 1900年后，特斯拉在纽约继续他的研究，包括著名的沃登克里弗塔项目，这是一个旨在实现全球无线通信和能量传输的巨大塔楼。尽管该项目因资金不足而未能完成，但代表了特斯拉对全球无线通信的远见。晚年，他专注于研究死亡射线、遥控技术和地球物理武器等概念，并继续探索无线能量传输的可能性。尽管他的许多想法在当时被视为过于超前，但现代科技如雷达、卫星通信和无线充电等技术都印证了他的远见。1943年1月7日，特斯拉在纽约酒店孤独去世，留下了大量未发表的研究笔记和专利。
points.descriptionEn: After 1900, Tesla continued his research in New York, including the famous Wardenclyffe Tower project, a massive tower designed for global wireless communication and energy transmission. Though the project was abandoned due to lack of funding, it represented Tesla's vision for global wireless communication. In his later years, he focused on concepts like the death ray, remote control technology, and geophysical weapons, continuing to explore wireless power transmission possibilities. While many of his ideas were considered too advanced for his time, modern technologies such as radar, satellite communication, and wireless charging have vindicated his vision. Tesla died alone in a New York hotel on January 7, 1943, leaving numerous unpublished research notes and patents.

supporter.zh: 特斯拉是真正的天才发明家，他的交流电系统彻底改变了现代电力传输方式，为电气化时代奠定了基础。他不仅是一位工程师，更是一位远见卓识的梦想家，预见了无线通信、远程控制和全球能量传输的可能性。特斯拉的发明包括交流电动机、特斯拉线圈、无线通信系统等，这些技术至今仍在广泛应用。他的科学精神和创新思维激励着一代又一代的科学家和工程师，是科技史上最具影响力的人物之一。
supporter.en: Tesla was a true genius inventor whose alternating current system revolutionized modern power transmission, laying the foundation for the electrical age. He was not just an engineer but a visionary dreamer who anticipated wireless communication, remote control, and global energy transmission. Tesla's inventions include the AC motor, Tesla coil, and wireless communication systems, technologies still widely used today. His scientific spirit and innovative thinking continue to inspire generations of scientists and engineers, making him one of the most influential figures in technological history.

critic.zh: 特斯拉的批评者指出他过于理想主义，缺乏商业头脑，导致许多重要发明未能商业化。他与爱迪生的电流战争虽然胜利，但也消耗了大量资源。特斯拉晚年的一些想法如死亡射线被视为不切实际，甚至有人质疑他后期研究的科学性。此外，他在财务上的失败和晚年贫困也反映了他在商业管理上的不足。批评者认为，尽管特斯拉是一位天才发明家，但他在将科学发现转化为实际应用方面存在明显缺陷。
critic.en: Critics of Tesla point out that he was overly idealistic and lacked business acumen, leading to many of his important inventions never being commercialized. His current war with Edison, though victorious, consumed significant resources. Some of his later ideas, like the death ray, were seen as impractical, and some questioned the scientific validity of his later research. Additionally, his financial failures and poverty in later life reflect deficiencies in his business management. Critics argue that while Tesla was a genius inventor, he had clear shortcomings in translating scientific discoveries into practical applications.

objective.zh: 历史学界和流行文化中，特斯拉被塑造为被低估的天才与科学先知的形象。他的故事体现了科学进步与商业竞争的复杂关系。特斯拉的遗产超越了他的具体发明，他象征着创新精神与远见卓识。在流行文化中，他常被描绘为与爱迪生形成对比的孤独天才形象，代表着纯粹的科学追求。现代研究表明，特斯拉的许多想法确实具有前瞻性，他的无线通信和能量传输理论为后来的技术发展提供了重要启示。特斯拉的一生反映了天才与时代、理想与现实之间的永恒张力。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Tesla has been portrayed as an underrated genius and scientific prophet. His story illustrates the complex relationship between scientific progress and commercial competition. Tesla's legacy extends beyond his specific inventions; he symbolizes innovative spirit and visionary thinking. In popular culture, he is often depicted as a lonely genius figure contrasting with Edison, representing pure scientific pursuit. Modern research confirms that many of Tesla's ideas were indeed ahead of their time, with his theories on wireless communication and energy transmission providing crucial insights for later technological developments. Tesla's life reflects the eternal tension between genius and era, ideal and reality.

self.zh: 我的发明属于全世界，它们是人类共同财富。
self.en: My inventions belong to the world, they are the common property of mankind.

others.zh: 如果特斯拉的成就被完全理解，那么当今世界将视他为比托马斯·爱迪生更伟大的发明家，比亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔更重要的通信先驱。
others.en: If Tesla's achievements were fully understood, the world today would view him as a greater inventor than Thomas Edison and a more important pioneer in communications than Alexander Graham Bell.
